# Ingest sequence by source kind (a repository and a document)

One ingestion pathway, two sequences. A repository and a document pass the same gates (capture, staging, the batch, acceptance), but their content is split into different layers of detail, and the stages do different work on each. Owner, 26 November: an unlicensed repository is treated the same as any external source. Its licence status is a label recorded with its provenance, and never a reason to hold, withhold or block it at any stage. Work that uses it cites it, as it cites every external source: that is a provenance rule, applied when the work is written, not a gate on ingestion. The unit names and relation rules are those of src/resource_librarian/dik.py; the to-be steps are proposed and unaccepted.

## The stages for each kind

| Stage | A repository (code) | A document (PDF, paper, long text) | Where in the to-be |
|---|---|---|---|
| Authorship and licence | own code, or an external source (third-party authorship); an unlicensed repository is an external source like any other, its licence status a label | own documents, research documents or third-party, from the folder's purpose | `folder-review:folderscreen` |
| Capture | the README and the tree at a commit, the licence id where there is one; a nested repository is its own source | the immutable file, with its literal header and DOI metadata | `source-intake:capture` |
| Parse | a syntax tree per file, by script (tree-sitter, Python AST); no model call | the text with its page map; conversion or OCR where needed, by a Clerk and reviewed by a Scribe | `source-parse:parse`, `source-parse:convplan` |
| Data: the finest units | files, modules (each listing up to 25 of its symbols), entry points, endpoints, settings, languages, dependencies | chapters or sections, then chunks for reading | `source-reading:data` |
| Reading | bounded reading of the components that need describing; most structure is scripted | bounded chunk reading by Clerks, then a whole-document pass | `source-reading:read` |
| Relations: Information | static structure only (imports, routes), by script; never runtime behaviour | document order, and chapter relations a Scribe proposes from two or more read chapters, marked inferred | `source-reading:relateskip`, `source-reading:relate` |
| The note: Knowledge | Components, How It Fits Together | Chapters, the Bottom Line | `source-reading:review` |
| Graph | a code graph, through the folder group's application in Geo-Grapher | the paper graph, once a PDF is fully converted | `folder-review:folderapply`, `paper-publication:dpub` |

## The layers of detail

| Layer | A repository | A document |
|---|---|---|
| Source | the repository at a commit | the document at its capture |
| Component | a module, package or entry point | a chapter or section |
| Unit | a file; a module's functions and classes are symbols listed on its module record (dik.py keeps at most 25), not records of their own | a chunk or page |
| Claim | a static relation or a described behaviour, cited by its locator | a claim with its verbatim quote |
| Proposed expansion, not in dik.py | a function or class as a Data record of its own, so a claim can cite it directly and a module's symbols past the 25th are kept | none needed: a page is already a unit |

## Rules

- A document-level claim needs document-level coverage: a chapter not read has no relations drawn to it (dik.py).
- A repository's relations are static structure, never runtime behaviour (dik.py).
- Third-party material, an unlicensed repository included, is read-only and shares the library's third-party graphs by default (folder_review.py READ_ONLY, suggested_graph).
- Licence status alone never holds a folder (`folder-review:dfolderauth`). What can hold one is separate: a scope the caller was not granted, content linked from outside the roots, a sensitivity flag, or another reserved decision; the Clerk's screen settles authorship.
- Attribution is a provenance rule: work that uses an external source cites it. It applies when the work is written, and never blocks capture, reading or acceptance.
